title: Bo Pieter Johannes Andree | Data Scientist, Development Data Group, World Bank
gist: A World Bank staff-profile page for data scientist Bo Andree, architect of the Bank's weekly Real-Time Food Prices dataset and World Food Security Outlook (which feeds the Crisis Response Window and the UN Famine Action Mechanism), whose post titles run from 'Global hunger nears one billion' (July 2026) to 'Global food security monitoring goes dark' (August 2026) — suggesting both rising hunger and a degrading real-time monitoring capacity in mid-2026.

insights.claim: Bo Andree leads the World Bank's 'Real-Time Food Prices' dataset, described as a live compilation updated weekly through a combination of direct measurement and AI imputation, built specifically to monitor food prices in fragile and data-scarce settings.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: A concrete, named weekly AI-augmented food-price dataset — directly useful as a leading indicator for food-commodity and food-insecurity-driven macro/political risk in fragile states.
insights.locator: He spearheads the Real-Time Food Prices dataset—a live compilation updated weekly through direct measurement and AI imputation.

insights.claim: Andree manages the World Bank's 'World Food Security Outlook,' which the text states 'has been central to establishing and replenishing the World Bank's Crisis Response Window' — directly linking his real-time monitoring work to the Bank's crisis-financing trigger mechanism.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Establishes a direct causal chain from a specific data product to a specific crisis-financing facility — relevant for understanding what data triggers World Bank emergency food-crisis funding releases.
insights.quote: central to establishing and replenishing the World Bank's Crisis Response Window
insights.locator: manages the World Food Security Outlook

insights.claim: Andree's earlier academic work with Aart Kraay on 'Predicting Food Crises' 'helped shape the Bank's approach to famine early warning under the Famine Action Mechanism,' per the text — tying academic forecasting research directly to institutional famine-response policy.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Links a specific research paper to a specific institutional early-warning system — useful provenance for anyone assessing the Famine Action Mechanism's methodological basis.
insights.quote: helped shape the Bank's approach to famine early warning under the Famine Action Mechanism
insights.locator: His earlier work with Aart Kraay on Predicting Food Crises

themes.theme: A Deteriorating 2026 Signal in the Post Titles

insights.claim: Andree's most recent post, dated August 4, 2026, is titled 'Global food security monitoring goes dark,' immediately following a July 21, 2026 post titled 'Global hunger nears one billion' — the sequence of titles alone suggests both worsening global hunger and a degrading capacity to monitor it in real time as of mid-2026, though the article text itself does not elaborate on the content of either post.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: A titles-only signal (not elaborated in this record) that global hunger monitoring infrastructure itself may be at risk in mid-2026 — worth following up the linked posts directly for the underlying cause (funding, data-source loss, etc.) before treating as confirmed.
insights.locator: Global food security monitoring goes dark, August 04, 2026

insights.claim: Andree has led food and nutrition security analytics and trade-monitoring projects across 25+ countries combining machine learning, geospatial analysis and real-time data systems, and advises UN-FAO on advanced technologies and AI for food security classification.
insights.speaker: World Bank Blogs
insights.so_what: Shows direct institutional cross-pollination between World Bank real-time data tools and UN-FAO's food-security classification systems (e.g. IPC-type frameworks).
insights.locator: serves as an adviser to UN-FAO on advanced technologies and AI for food security classification
